## The challenge

The four Lenses showed costs, harms, hidden labor, and incentives. Most of them are not in the hands of one researcher. Panarchy asks where change is possible, and at which level. The common question of the afternoon is:

> **What changes across interconnected levels would make generative AI use in academic research more responsible?**

Each participant turns this question into their own **challenge**. Start from your Research Use Card. Write one sentence: what must change so that your Research Use becomes more responsible? Your Research Use stays the same all day. The challenge names the change that you look for.

## What Panarchy is

[Panarchy](https://www.liberatingstructures.com/panarchy) is one of the Liberating Structures. With it, a group identifies "opportunities and obstacles for spreading ideas at multiple levels" of its environment [@ls-panarchy]. The idea comes from the study of social-ecological systems [@holling2001]:

- Small, local levels change fast. A research project can change its practice next week.
- Large levels change slowly. A university, an industry, or a law changes over years.
- The levels influence each other in both directions. A local experiment can spread upwards. Resources and rules from a large level shape what is possible below.

**Discover your own levels.** You decide which levels matter for your challenge. The list below is only an illustration. Do not copy it.

> individual research project → research group or department → university and research sector → model vendors and industry → regulation and society

Original diagram, adapted from Liberating Structures Panarchy under CC BY-SA 4.0.](../assets/handouts/panarchy-chart-sheet.svg){fig-alt="Panarchy Chart for one participant. An arrow on the left points up: ideas and experiments spread up. An arrow on the right points down: resources and rules flow down."}lock 1: from your challenge to a group Action Plan {#block-1}

You work alone, in pairs, and in groups of four. Use Sheet 1, back, and Sheet 2, front, part A.

| Step | Minutes | Format  | What you do                                                                                                            |
| ---: | ------: | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|    1 |      15 | Alone   | Frame the challenge and identify influences. Write the challenge in the header of the Panarchy Chart. List influences. |
|    2 |      20 | Pairs   | Translate the influences into levels on your Panarchy Chart. Name each level. Compare your levels.                     |
|    3 |       5 | Plenary | Form new groups of four. Choose people who were not in your Lens group.                                                |
|    4 |      15 | Groups  | Each person presents their challenge and their Panarchy Chart.                                                         |
|    5 |       5 | Groups  | Select one challenge for deeper analysis. The other challenges stay open for Block 2.                                  |
|    6 |      10 | Alone   | Identify Opportunities & Barriers for the selected challenge. Note the level of each.                                  |
|    7 |      25 | Groups  | Discuss and prioritize. Consolidate the findings into one group Action Plan on a flipchart or in a shared document.    |
|      |      10 | Groups  | Buffer: complete the group Action Plan.                                                                                |

: Panarchy Block 1 {.striped}

Keep your Panarchy Chart. You need it in Block 2.

An **opportunity** is a place where a change at one level can unlock a change at another level. A **barrier** is a place where one level blocks another. A level higher on the chart does not always hold more power.

## Block 2: the open challenges {#block-2}

After the afternoon break, form new pairs across the groups of Block 1. Do not pair with a person who already discussed your challenge with you. Each pair examines the challenges that Block 1 did not select:

- **Two open challenges:** examine the Opportunities & Barriers for both.
- **One open challenge:** both of you examine that challenge.

| Step | Minutes | Format | What you do                                                                                  |
| ---: | ------: | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|    1 |      10 | Alone  | Identify Opportunities & Barriers for the open challenge or challenges. Use Sheet 2, part B. |
|    2 |      35 | Pairs  | Discuss and prioritize. Record the findings and possible actions for each open challenge.    |

: Panarchy Block 2 {.striped}

Use the existing Panarchy Charts. Every challenge receives an in-depth discussion, in Block 1 or in Block 2.

## Individual Action Plan {#action-plan}

Every participant leaves with an individual Action Plan for their own Research Use. Use Sheet 2, back.

| Minutes | Format  | What you do                                                                                                          |
| ------: | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|      20 | Alone   | Complete the Action Plan: the intended change, the next step, the barriers, the timeline, and the success indicator. |
|      10 | Pairs   | Peer review. Is the next step concrete? Is the timeline realistic? Would the success indicator show the change?      |
|      15 | Plenary | Course evaluation and closing.                                                                                       |

: The individual Action Plan {.striped}

The Action Plan prepares the follow-up task: the [Responsible GenAI Use Statement](assignments.qmd).

The [fictional example](handouts/panarchy-example.qmd) shows a completed chart. Its content is invented.

## What you produce

- Your own **Panarchy Chart** with your challenge, your influences, and named levels.
- **Opportunities & Barriers** for your challenge, from Block 1 or from Block 2.
- A **group Action Plan** for the challenge that your group of four selected in Block 1.
- Your **individual Action Plan** for your own Research Use, reviewed by a peer.

## Paper, documents, and flipcharts are enough

The exercise needs no online whiteboard, no account, and no sticky notes.

- Two double-sided A4 sheets for each participant, on paper or as editable files.
- A flipchart or a shared document for each group of four.

Take a photo of a flipchart if the group wants to keep it. Do not photograph people without their consent.
